milestone: Managed String fields in immutable CPU records

implementation.source: String fields alongside finite nested records, Bool and numeric/Bool collections; construction/access/immutable updates, imported helpers, record arrays/maps, callback captures and CPU worker arguments/results
implementation.layout: String descriptor counts as three inline storage units; existing nominal identities, cycle rejection and depth/expanded-layout budgets remain checked
implementation.lowering: Declare String runtime support from record schemas even without direct String expressions; validate nested String fields at ordinary record helper entries/results
implementation.ownership: Recursive record and record-array packet/result retention calls the existing checked String retain operation before publication; failed later fields settle partial owners
implementation.limits: Direct String arrays and String-valued map results remain gated; no whole-record CLI display, GPU/distributed records or public C/C++ interface introduced

coverage: Exact Unicode/NUL text in shared nested String descriptors and exact raw-bit numeric siblings; canonical empty fields
Immutable nested updates, scalar queries/index/slice, conditional records, imported helpers, record arrays/maps and nested whole-record captures
All six numeric families and mixed Bool-array/numeric-array/tensor fields alongside Strings
Source settlement before scheduling, nested/cached worker results, repeated observations, group release and retained result after scheduler destruction
Malformed/oversized/noncanonical/unknown-owner String fields and malformed numeric siblings reject before publication; earlier retained owners settle
All field-owner allocation positions, cancellation/deadlines, admission budget and scheduler allocation failure; successful shared backing is not copied
String-record TaskError recovery/rethrow and managed diagnostic text in retained fields
Strict field types, forged IR, String descriptor layout units, cycle rejection and preservation of rejected executable/MLIR/LLVM outputs
Documentation example compiled and executed in each variant
Existing record arrays, Bool fields, numeric record workers, standalone String workers, task recovery and frontend/continuation regressions
qualification.scope: Focused CPU qualification, not a full-suite or fresh GPU execution claim. Optimized applies to generated programs and harnesses with the existing runtime archive.
qualification.build_notes: No production source changes after the successful focused run. Existing frontend tests freshly relinked; regression programs use current compiler/runtime. An early development smoke assertion was corrected to allow balanced cleanup diagnostics on successful numeric-array output before final qualification.
